# British International School Hanoi: Review
UK National Curriculum, EYFS, IB DP, IGCSE, IPC
...
BIS Hanoi takes students aged 18 months to 18 years through its pre-school, primary school, and secondary school.
The early years section follows the UK’s Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) for children aged 18 months to five years, which means you can expect a wide variety of fun, play-based activities, held both indoors and outdoors.
*The primary school combines the National Curriculum for England and the International Primary Curriculum (IPC) for Years 1 through to 6.*
...
The *British-style of education* continues in the first few years of secondary school, from Years 7 to 11.
The curriculum includes English, maths, science, geography, history, PSHE (Personal, Social, Health, and Economic Education), design technology, digital literacy, languages (Thai, Mandarin, French, and Spanish), PE, drama, music, and art.
*Students take their IGCSEs in Year 11.
Learning then switches to the International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme (IBDP) in Years 12 and 13.*
...
Average school fees are **VND 731.5m** per year.
Additional charges may include registration, enrolment and transport fees.
...

content.text:
## BIS Hanoi vs UNIS Hanoi

Both are established, English-medium international schools in Hanoi, serving students from early years through secondary. The main difference is the educational pathway: **BIS offers a British-style route that leads into the IB Diploma**, while **UNIS is an IB school throughout**.

| | **BIS Hanoi** | **UNIS Hanoi** |
|---|---|---|
| **Curriculum** | English National Curriculum and International Primary Curriculum in primary; IGCSEs in Years 10–11; IB Diploma in Years 12–13. | IB curriculum across the school, from early years through Grade 12. |
| **Best fit if…** | Your child is used to, or would benefit from, a British-style structure and subject pathway before the IB Diploma. | You want a consistent IB approach throughout schooling, with less of a curriculum shift between stages. |
| **2026–27 tuition** | Annual fees range from **VND 253.6 million** for F1 half-day to **VND 970.2 million** for Years 12–13. Years 1–4 are about **VND 657.6–715.5 million**. | Annual-payment fees range from **USD 17,460** for Early Years 3–4 to **USD 39,870** for Grades 11–12. Grades 1–5 cost **USD 33,330**; Grades 6–8, **USD 35,210**. |
| **What tuition includes** | The published fee schedule says tuition includes items such as uniforms, daily lunches, learning materials, day trips, and required secondary examination fees. | The listed tuition is in USD; compare the school’s full fee schedule for deposits, payment terms, and other charges. |
| **Age/grade structure** | Foundation through Year 13. | Early Years through Grade 12. |

### What to weigh up

- **Curriculum continuity:** UNIS is the clearer choice if you specifically want an all-IB education. BIS may suit a student who prefers the more subject-structured British/IGCSE progression, while still offering the IB Diploma in the final years.
- **Cost comparison:** The fee figures use different currencies and grade systems, so compare the exact year your child would enter and the total cost after fees and deposits. BIS publishes fees in VND; UNIS publishes them in USD.
- **Admissions and day-to-day fit:** Ask both schools about availability in the relevant grade, class placement, language support, transport, extracurriculars, and any one-time or refundable charges. A campus visit and a conversation with each school are especially useful, since teaching style and community can matter as much as curriculum.

**In short:** choose **BIS** for a British-to-IB pathway; consider **UNIS** for an IB pathway from early years onward. The best choice depends on your child’s learning style, likely future school destinations, and the specific grade-level costs.
